Probe false-sets are size 3, so a clause C (size 3, positive) is false on a probe iff C ⊆ F_probe. With 128 probes each a random 3-subset, only 128 of the 1140 triples are "covered" → only those clauses pass condition 5 → ~123. Right.

The DFS cost: how many nodes were visited? The pruning on `psig == ALLPROBE` happens early. Since positive literals are true on most probes, a clause of 3 positive literals has psig = all probes where at least one literal is true — a probe fails only if all 3 atoms are false there. So psig becomes ALLPROBE quickly (after 2-3 literals, most clauses are true on all probes → pruned!). That's why it's fast: the psig pruning is very effective here.

So the worst case for DFS cost is when clauses remain false on some probe — i.e., probes have large false-sets. Let me make probes have false-sets of size 19 (nearly everything false) — then every clause is false on probe 0 → condition 5 always satisfied → no pruning from psig.

But wait: if probes have false-set of size 19, then only 1 atom is true per probe. Clause {i,j,k} is false on that probe iff all of i,j,k are false → since only 1 atom is true, yes for most triples. So condition 5 is satisfied for most clauses → no psig pruning. Then the DFS cost = full 87440 nodes with condition-4 checks. Let me build that variant: probes = contexts where all atoms are false except one (or even all false → every clause false on every probe → signature 0 for all → single class with all members!).

If all probes have ALL atoms false, then every clause is false on every probe → all eligible clauses have signature 0 → one class. Then queries: for the single class, "all members false" vs "some member false". That's also a good stress for the query aggregation (all members in one class).

Let me also double check: with all-atoms-false probes, condition 5 is satisfied for every clause → the DFS explores everything with condition-4 checks at every node. This is the true worst case for enumeration cost.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Worst-case DFS: probes make every clause false (no psig pruning),
training false-sets are all pairs so width-3 clauses pass conditions 3+4."""
import json, random, sys

rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 7)
NATOMS = 20
NSRC = 16
schema = [{'name': 'f%d' % i, 'type': 'FLAG'} for i in range(NATOMS)]
atoms = [{'cmp': 'eq', 'left': {'field': 'f%d' % i, 'at': 0},
          'right': {'const': True, 'type': 'FLAG'}} for i in range(NATOMS)]
pairs = [(i, j) for i in range(NATOMS) for j in range(i + 1, NATOMS)]

def row(false_set):
    vals = [True] * NATOMS
    for i in false_set:
        vals[i] = False
    return vals

train = []
t = 0
for s in range(NSRC):
    fs = list(pairs); rng.shuffle(fs)
    extra = [rng.choice(pairs) for _ in range(66)]
    rows = [{'t': t + k, 'values': row(f)} for k, f in enumerate(fs + extra)]
    t += len(rows)
    train.append({'id': 'tr%d' % s, 'source': 'src%d' % s, 'rows': rows})

# every probe context: all atoms false -> every clause is false on every probe
probes = [{'id': 'pr0', 'source': 'src0',
           'rows': [{'t': i, 'values': [False] * NATOMS} for i in range(128)]}]
queries = []
t = 0
for q in range(4):
    rows = [{'t': t + c, 'values': row(tuple(sorted(rng.sample(range(NATOMS), rng.randint(0, 4))))}
            for c in range(256)]
    t += 256
    queries.append({'id': 'qr%d' % q, 'source': 'src0', 'rows': rows})

req = {'version': 1, 'schema': schema, 'window': 1, 'atoms': atoms,
       'policy': {'max_width': 4, 'min_support': 1, 'min_witness': 1},
       'train': train, 'probes': probes, 'queries': queries}
json.dump(req, open(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'stress2.json', 'w'))
print('ok')
PYEOF
cd /app/dev && python3 stress2.py 7 stress2.json && (time /app/submission/run.sh < stress2.json > out2.json) 2>&1 | tail -4; python3 -c "
import json;r=json.load(open('/app/dev/out2.json'));print('classes',len(r['classes']),'members',sum(c['members'] for c in r['classes']));print('q0',r['queries'][0]);print('sig',[c['signature'] for c in r['classes']][:3])"
